Which two circuit quantities can never jump at a switching instant, and why?
column2: Capacitor voltage and inductor current: a jump would need infinite current (\(i = C\,dv/dt\)) or infinite voltage (\(v = L\,di/dt\)) — i.e., stored energy changing in zero time.

column1: DC steady-state models of C and L?
column2: Capacitor → open circuit; inductor → short circuit.

column1: Time constant of an RC circuit? Of an RL circuit?
column2: \(\tau = R_{Th}C\); \(\tau = L/R_{Th}\), with \(R_{Th}\) seen by the storage element (independent sources off).

column1: Why does a larger R speed up an RL transient but slow an RC one?
column2: In RL the resistor dissipates the inductor's energy (faster with larger R); in RC it throttles the charging current (slower with larger R).

column1: The master formula for any variable in a first-order circuit?
column2: \(x(t) = x(\infty) + [x(t_0^+) - x(\infty)]\,e^{-(t-t_0)/\tau}\) — same τ for every variable.

column1: How do you find the initial value of a NON-state variable (e.g., a resistor current) after switching?
column2: Draw the \(t_0^+\) circuit with C replaced by a voltage source \(v_C(t_0^+)\) (or L by a current source \(i_L(t_0^+)\)) and solve it.

column1: Percent complete after 1, 2, 3, 5 time constants?
50% delay of a first-order step response?
column2: \(\tau\ln 2 \approx 0.693\tau\).

column1: 10–90% rise time of a single pole, and its link to bandwidth?
column2: \(t_r = \tau\ln 9 \approx 2.2\tau = 0.35/f_{3dB}\).

column1: Settling time to within ε of final value?
column2: \(t = \tau\ln(1/\varepsilon)\); 0.1% takes 6.9τ.

column1: Settling time for an N-bit ADC (½ LSB, full-scale step)?
column2: \((N+1)\ln 2\cdot\tau\): 9.0τ at 12 bits, 11.8τ at 16 bits.

column1: Energy lost charging a capacitor from 0 to V through a resistor?
column2: ½CV² — exactly half of the CV² drawn from the source, independent of R.

column1: CMOS dynamic power formula and its origin?
column2: \(P = \alpha C V_{DD}^2 f\): each 0→1→0 cycle draws \(CV_{DD}^2\) from the supply regardless of transistor strength.

column1: How can you charge a capacitor with less than ½CV² loss?
column2: Charge it in N steps (loss CV²/2N) or with a slow ramp (adiabatic charging) so the resistor never sees a large voltage.

column1: Square-wave (0/V, 50% duty) steady state through an RC: \(V_{max}\), \(V_{min}\)?
column2: With \(\rho = e^{-T/2\tau}\): \(V_{max} = V/(1+\rho)\), \(V_{min} = V\rho/(1+\rho)\); ripple ≈ \(VT/(4\tau)\) when \(T \ll \tau\).

column1: General solution of \(\tau\dot x + x = u(t)\)?
column2: \(x(t) = x(0)e^{-t/\tau} + \frac{1}{\tau}\int_0^t e^{-(t-\lambda)/\tau}u(\lambda)\,d\lambda\) — an exponentially weighted average of past inputs (a convolution).

column1: Ramp response of a first-order low-pass in steady state?
column2: It tracks the ramp (slope m) delayed by τ, with constant error mτ.

column1: What happens when you interrupt an inductor's current with no flyback path?
column2: \(v = L\,di/dt\) grows as large as needed — switch arcs or transistor breaks down.

column1: Resistor vs diode flyback across an inductive load: tradeoff?
column2: Resistor: faster decay (τ = L/R) but switch sees supply + I₀R. Diode: switch sees supply + 0.7 V but slow decay (slower relay release).

column1: Ideal inverting op-amp integrator output?
column2: \(v_{out} = v_{out}(0) - \frac{1}{RC}\int v_{in}\,dt\); add \(R_f \parallel C\) (leaky integrator: τ = \(R_fC\), DC gain \(-R_f/R\)) to stop it drifting into the rail.

column1: kT/C noise at 300 K for 1 pF? Does it depend on R?
column2: ≈ 64 µV rms; no — it depends only on C (and T).

column1: The central tradeoff in an ADC sampling capacitor?
column2: Bigger C → lower kT/C noise but longer settling (τ = RC) → needs a stronger driver or more time.

column1: Why does on-chip wire delay grow with the square of length?
column2: Both R and C are proportional to length, so RC ∝ length²; repeaters break long wires into segments.

column1: Two equal capacitors, one at V₀, connected through R: final voltage and energy lost?
column2: \(V_0/2\) each; half the initial energy (\(\tfrac14 CV_0^2\)) is lost, independent of R.

column1: What does a negative Thevenin resistance seen by a capacitor mean?
column2: τ = R_Th·C is negative: the response grows as \(e^{+t/|\tau|}\) (positive feedback) until something saturates — the regenerative action of latches and comparators.

column1: Why can a bare resistor across a relay coil be a bad flyback design?
column2: It conducts the whole time the coil is energized, wasting power and loading the switch; put a diode in series with it (or use a diode + Zener).
